publication.inid_54_title: Bromine-containing argyrodite solid electrolyte with suppressed lithium chloride impurity and improved moisture stability
publication.inid_57_abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein a = x + y, 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5. Replacing part of the chlorine with bromine expands the lattice and raises the anion disorder on the 4a and 4d sites, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway, while the halogen-rich composition is fired at 460 degrees C to 520 degrees C so that a lithium chloride impurity phase does not precipitate. In an X-ray diffraction pattern measured with CuK-alpha radiation, the ratio of the peak intensity at 2-theta = 34.8 degrees attributed to LiCl to the peak intensity at 30.0 degrees attributed to the argyrodite phase is 0.05 or less. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 7 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, retains 85% or more of the conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, and keeps the argyrodite phase without a glass ceramic by-product. Compared with Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 type conductors, the material gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
claims: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)X(a), wherein X is at least one halogen selected from Cl, Br, and I, and 1.0 <= a <= 2.0.
2. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.6.
3. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.40.
4. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, having an ionic conductivity of 7 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.
5. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a retention of ionic conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 85% or more.
6. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte is in the form of particles having a median particle diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
7. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the ratio IA/IB is 0.02 or less.
8. A positive electrode layer for an all-solid-state battery, comprising a positive electrode active material and the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

9. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

10. A method of manufacturing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanically milling the mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 460 degrees C to 520 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the firing is performed for 2 hours to 8 hours.

publication.inid_54_title: Sulfide glass ceramic solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 crystal phase with controlled crystallinity and widened electrochemical window
publication.inid_57_abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte is a glass ceramic in which a Li7P3S11 crystal phase is precipitated in a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 70:30 and containing LiI in an amount of 3 mol% to 8 mol%. A glass obtained by mechanical amorphization of the raw materials in a planetary mill is heat-treated at 260 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours, just above the crystallization onset, so that the metastable Li7P3S11 phase precipitates with a crystallite size of 30 nm to 150 nm while devitrification to the low-conductivity Li4P2S6 phase is kept to 3% or less. The degree of crystallinity is 60% to 85%, the residual glassy phase deforms plastically during cold pressing, and the glass ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 4.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C with an activation energy of 0.22 eV. The iodide widens the electrochemical window on the reduction side to 1.6 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic is distinguished from crystalline Li6PS5Cl or Li3PS4 powders by the presence of the vitreous phase and gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life.

publication.inid_54_title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and tin substitution for improved moisture stability
publication.inid_57_abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid is a crystallized glass comprising a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 75:25 in which 2 mol% to 6 mol% of the phosphorus is substituted by tin, and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated from the matrix. A glassy precursor prepared by melt quenching at 750 degrees C is reheated at 240 degrees C to 280 degrees C so that the beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 100 nm and a degree of crystallinity of 50% to 75%. The tin, a soft acid, binds the sulfur more strongly than phosphorus, and the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 60 minutes is 8 cm3/g or less. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and retains 80% or more of the conductivity after the exposure. Unlike crystalline Li7P3S11 or Li6PS5Cl powders, the remaining vitreous phase gives good deformability, and an all-solid-state battery using the material shows improved cycle life.

publication.inid_54_title: Fine-particle argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor with controlled halogen occupancy for positive electrode mixtures
publication.inid_57_abstract: An argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)X(1+x), wherein X is Cl or a combination of Cl and Br and 0.3 <= x <= 0.6, and is in the form of particles having a median particle diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 2.0 micrometers and a specific surface area of 3 m2/g to 12 m2/g. The particles are produced by firing a precursor obtained by ball milling Li2S, P2S5, and LiCl at 480 degrees C to 540 degrees C and then wet pulverizing the fired product in heptane with zirconia beads of 0.3 mm, which keeps the chlorine occupancy of the 4a site at 70% or more and avoids the amorphization that occurs in dry milling. The fine particles fill the gaps between positive electrode active material particles, so that a positive electrode mixture containing the particles in an amount of 20 wt% to 30 wt% shows a lower tortuosity and a higher utilization of the active material. The ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, and the positive electrode mixture has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more. Compared with coarse Li7P3S11 or Li3PS4 powders, the material improves the rate capability and cycle life of an all-solid-state battery.

publication.inid_54_title: High-conductivity argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor with a lithium-deficient composition and an impurity-free diffraction pattern
publication.inid_57_abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a lithium-deficient composition represented by Li(6-x-y)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.5 and 0 < y <= 0.15, the lithium deficiency y being introduced by adding P2S5 in a slight excess so that lithium vacancies are created on the 48h site. The anion disorder between the sulfur and chlorine sites is 40% or more, no diffraction peak attributable to LiCl, Li3PS4, or Li2S is observed, and the lattice parameter is 9.80 angstroms to 9.86 angstroms. The combination of the vacancies and the anion disorder gives an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C for a cold-pressed pellet and 9 mS/cm or more for a pellet sintered at 500 degrees C, together with an activation energy of 0.26 eV or less. The material is crystalline and is not a glass ceramic, so that its conductivity does not decrease upon storage at 60 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor widens the electrochemical window of a positive electrode mixture compared with Li10GeP2S12 and Li7P3S11, and an all-solid-state battery using the material in the separator layer and the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability.

claims: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a composition represented by Li(6-x-y)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.5 and 0 < y <= 0.15, wherein no diffraction peak attributable to LiCl, Li3PS4, or Li2S is observed in an X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C measured on a pellet cold-pressed at 370 MPa.
2. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.45.
3. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein 0.03 <= y <= 0.10.
4. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein an anion disorder between the sulfur site and the chlorine site determined by Rietveld refinement is 40% or more.
5. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, having a lattice parameter of 9.80 angstroms to 9.86 angstroms.
6. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, having an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.26 eV or less.
7. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein an ionic conductivity of a pellet sintered at 500 degrees C is 9 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.
8. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein a decrease in ionic conductivity after storage at 60 degrees C for 30 days in argon is 5% or less.
9. A positive electrode mixture comprising a positive electrode active material coated with lithium niobate and the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.

10. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer comprising the positive electrode mixture of claim 9, a negative electrode layer, and a separator layer comprising the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.

11. A method of manufacturing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and LiCl such that P2S5 is in excess by 1 mol% to 5 mol% relative to the stoichiometric composition; mechanically milling the mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the firing is performed for 4 hours to 12 hours.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the mechanical milling is performed in a planetary mill at 400 rpm to 600 rpm.
